Step 12: Biological Transition Flow

Method: Soft assignment computes how source cells are mapped to target archetype neighborhoods by the flow model. For each source cell, the transported position is projected onto the target archetype simplex. The resulting matrix shows the expected archetype composition of transported cells, revealing differentiation trajectory structure.

Discrete transition matrix: source cells are transported via the learned flow field, then assigned to the nearest archetype by Euclidean distance in PCA space. Row = source archetype (pre-transport assignment), column = target archetype (post-transport nearest).

Step 13: Gene Alignment Along Flow

Gene-flow alignment: cosine similarity between each gene's PCA loading vector and the mean flow velocity. Positive = gene expression changes in the same direction as the flow (not necessarily upregulated -- it means the gene's variation axis aligns with the transport direction). Negative = expression changes in the opposite direction. Flow-aligned != upregulated: a gene can be flow-aligned because it decreases monotonically along the trajectory, if that decrease is the dominant direction.
